title: Jablková povidla (Apple Butter)
description: Prepared with apples.
steps: For one bushel of apples, use one gallon of cooked sweet must from the press.

Put enough apples in the must so they are submerged.
When soft, remove with a skimmer and add fresh ones, continuing until all apples are cooked.
Mash and return to the pot, cook over gentle heat with constant stirring.
A wooden spoon is best for this.
About one hour before it is done, add spices to taste—some cinnamon, clove, and allspice.
This butter takes considerable effort as it must be cooked until very thick, but it is then good and quite inexpensive.

title: Jahodový koláč (Strawberry Shortcake)
description: Prepared with strawberries, flour, and baking powder.
steps: Put four cupfuls of flour into a bowl, add to it two teaspoons of baking powder, a little salt and mix well.
Add half a cupful of butter, finely crumbled, and three, until all the flour is well mixed with the butter.
Then add as much milk as needed to make a not too stiff dough, similar to biscuit dough.

Dust the rolling pin with flour, turn the dough onto it, roll it out a little more, divide into two halves, grease the baking pan with butter, roll out one half of the dough about half a finger thick and line the pan with it, spread with butter and place the second half of the dough, also rolled out, on top and put into a nice hot oven to bake.
Let it bake well, which takes about half an hour, then turn out onto a board, split and let cool.
In the meantime, mash two quarts of strawberries with sugar.

When the cake has cooled, place one half on a plate, the broken (inner) side facing up, spread a nice thick layer of prepared strawberries over it, place the second half of the cake on top, again with the inner side facing up and spread a thick layer of strawberries over the top.

title: Karfiol pro Zimní Potřebu (Pickled Cauliflower)
description: Prepared with cauliflower, vinegar, and salt.
steps: Take young, tender cauliflower (which is most flavorful).
Clean it thoroughly and cut it into small pieces, about half an inch to an inch long.
Salt it well and let it sit for 16 hours.
Pour off the salt water and replace with fresh water, repeating this until all the salt is rinsed out.
Spread it on a colander to drain the water.

For every cup of vinegar, add an equal amount of sugar.
For every four cups of vinegar, add one spoon of mixed spices.
Bring everything to a boil.
Add the drained cauliflower (which must not be waterlogged) and boil well for 15 minutes.
Pack it hot into jars and seal well.

Alternatively, cauliflower preserved in mustard is also good: prepare as above but use less sugar and when it comes to a boil and has cooked for about 10 minutes, thicken it with mustard powder mixed in vinegar in a cup (to prevent lumps), and preserve like a sauce. This will be thicker. For one head of cauliflower use two cups of vinegar, one cup of sugar, a small teaspoon of mustard, and two large spoons of mustard powder.

Fold like a handkerchief and place on a plate
Let rest overnight
Early the next morning, roll out again to about noodle thickness
Cut into strips about a hand's width long and across
Cut the rectangles into squares and fold each into a cross pattern with ends meeting at the center, creating a four-pointed shape
Place on a buttered baking sheet and bake in an oven
When baked, spread jam on top, place on a platter, sprinkle with sugar, and serve

title: Krocan s nádivkou (Turkey with Sage Stuffing)
description: Prepared with turkey, sage, and bread.

Break two eggs into it, salt and pepper it
Add a piece of butter and enough milk to make the stuffing as thick as ordinary dumpling dough
Mix one spoonful of crushed and sifted sage into the stuffing

title: Krocan s nádivkou mandlovou (Turkey with Almond Stuffing)
description: Prepared with sour cream, almonds, and lemon rind.

ingredients.name: quarter pound of peeled and sliced almonds
a little ground flowers or herbs
small piece of lemon rind, finely chopped

steps: Beat two spoonfuls of fresh butter, crack two or three eggs into it
Pour in several spoonfuls of sour cream, a quarter pound of peeled and sliced almonds, a little ground flowers or herbs, a small piece of finely chopped lemon rind
Salt it, and if you want the stuffing slightly sweetened, add one spoonful of sugar
Add enough grated bread to make a sufficiently thick stuffing
Fill the cavity of a well-cleaned and eviscerated turkey with this, tie it up, salt it
Place the turkey on a roasting pan, pour several spoonfuls of broth underneath
Place pieces of butter on it and let it slowly roast on both sides until golden
However, you must frequently baste it with fresh butter
Then cut it, arrange neatly on a platter and pour over it the juices in which the turkey was roasted

title: Krocan s nádivkou z kaštanů (Turkey with Chestnut Stuffing)
description: Prepared with chestnuts, beef broth or water, and water.
steps: Peel two pounds of fine chestnuts
Place them in boiling water and leave them there until you can remove the thin skin with a clean cloth
Wash them and let them drain
Put four spoonfuls of butter on a platter, add two spoonfuls of ground sugar
Place near the fire and stir until the sugar turns slightly brown
Pour a little beef broth or water over it
Put the chestnuts in it and let them stew, but not completely tender, and especially make sure the chestnuts remain whole
Remove them and let them cool a little
Wash the well-cleaned and eviscerated turkey
When cooking be careful not to tear the cavity
Now fill the cavity with the chestnuts, sew or skewer it shut
Salt the turkey and roast according to the previous method
